title: Regulations and guidance publications
summary: Explains statutory and non-statutory regulations and guidance publications used by electricians, and the consequences of failing to comply with statutory Regulations.

sections.heading: Statutory and non-statutory regulations
paragraphs: Regulations are classified in two groups: statutory and non-statutory.
bullets: Statutory regulations
Non-statutory regulations

sections.heading: Key statutory regulations
paragraphs: The Health and Safety at Work etc. Act (HASAWA) is statutory and covers all places where work is carried out. The 'etc.' was added to cover voluntary work, etc. All persons are responsible for their own and others' safety.
bullets: Electricity at Work Regulations: require precautions to be taken against the risk of death or personal injury from electricity in work activities.
Electricity Safety, Quality and Continuity Regulations (ESQCR): cover the requirements for electricity supply in the United Kingdom.
Provision and Use of Work Equipment Regulations (PUWER): cover the supply and use of equipment in the workplace; equipment must be safe to use and be used safely by the operatives.

Control of Substances Hazardous to Health Regulations (COSHH): cover anything used in the workplace that could be considered hazardous to health, including chemicals, asbestos, cements, oils, sprays, etc.

Construction (Design and Management) Regulations (CDM): place specific duties on clients, designers and contractors so health and safety is considered throughout the life of a construction project, from inception to final demolition and removal.

sections.heading: More statutory regulations
paragraphs: These Regulations cover manual handling, protective equipment and noise.
bullets: Manual Handling Operations Regulations (MHOR): aim to reduce the very large incidence of injury and ill health caused by manual handling of loads at work.
Personal Protective Equipment at Work Regulations (PPEWR): require an assessment of PPE requirements; the employer supplies the PPE and the employee wears it.
Control of Noise at Work Regulations: place a duty on employers within Great Britain to reduce the risk to employees' health by controlling the noise they are exposed to.
Everyone at work could be exposed to noise and suffer temporary or permanent hearing loss; employers must eliminate or reduce noise levels.

sections.heading: Environmental and equality legislation
paragraphs: The Environmental Act is an Act of Parliament that defines the fundamental structure and authority for waste management and control of emissions into the environment.
The Disability Discrimination Act (DDA) has now been repealed and replaced by the Equality Act 2010, except in Northern Ireland where the DDA still applies.
bullets: DDA: formerly made it unlawful to discriminate against people because of their disabilities in employment, goods and services, education and transport.

Equality Act 2010: requires equal treatment in access to employment, and private and public services, regardless of age, disability, gender reassignment, marriage and civil partnership, race, religion or belief, sex and sexual orientation.

sections.heading: Non-statutory regulations and guidance
paragraphs: BS 7671 (Requirements for Electrical Installations) is non-statutory. It is based on the CENELEC harmonisation document, and in 1992 the IEE Wiring Regulations became British Standard BS 7671.
BS 7671 is published by the IET and is the national standard in the United Kingdom for low voltage electrical installations. It has closely followed the international standard IEC 60364.
bullets: On-Site Guide: a handbook containing some information not in BS 7671; a handy notebook reference for electricians.
Unite Union Book: published by the trade union 'Unite'; based on BS 7671; contains a wealth of information for the practising electrician.
IET Guidance Notes give additional clarification on how to implement and comply with BS 7671.
GN1: Selection and Erection (7th Edition)
GN2: Isolation and Switching (7th Edition)
GN3: Inspection and Testing (7th Edition)
GN4: Protection Against Fire (7th Edition)
GN5: Protection Against Electric Shock (7th Edition)
GN6: Protection Against Overcurrent (7th Edition)
GN7: Special Location (5th Edition)
GN8: Earthing and Bonding (3rd Edition)

sections.heading: Codes of practice
paragraphs: A code of practice is defined as 'a set of standards agreed on by a group of people who do a particular job' (Cambridge English Dictionary). Codes of practice give practical guidance on compliance.

They do not normally have the force of law, and failure to comply with an Approved Code of Practice is not an offence in itself. However, such a failure may contravene a statutory regulation which is enforceable by law.

sections.heading: Failure to comply with regulations
paragraphs: Breaking statutory Regulations has both direct and non-direct implications.
bullets: Direct: prosecution, fine, imprisonment.
Prohibition notice: a work activity or premises must not be used until the non-compliant situation is rectified.
Improvement notice: a work activity or premises can continue to be used, but shortcomings must be rectified within a specified time period.
Non-direct: dismissal, injury, death, loss of earnings, lost clients, loss of reputation.

flashcards.front: Why was 'etc.' added to the Health and Safety at Work etc. Act (HASAWA)?
flashcards.back: To cover voluntary work, etc. The Act is statutory and covers all places where work is carried out.
Electricity Safety, Quality and Continuity Regulations cover the requirements for electricity supply in the United Kingdom.
Provision and Use of Work Equipment Regulations: the supply and use of equipment in the workplace. Equipment must be safe to use and used safely by operatives.
Anything used in the workplace that could be hazardous to health, including chemicals, asbestos, cements, oils and sprays.

flashcards.front: What do the CDM Regulations require?
flashcards.back: Specific duties on clients, designers and contractors so health and safety is considered throughout a construction project, from inception to final demolition and removal.

flashcards.front: Under PPEWR, who supplies and who wears the PPE?
flashcards.back: The employer supplies the PPE and the employee wears it, after an assessment of PPE requirements has been carried out.

flashcards.front: Which Act replaced the Disability Discrimination Act (DDA)?
flashcards.back: The Equality Act 2010, except in Northern Ireland where the DDA still applies.

flashcards.front: What is BS 7671 and who publishes it?
flashcards.back: Requirements for Electrical Installations: the non-statutory national standard for low voltage installations in the UK, published by the IET.

flashcards.front: Which international standard has BS 7671 closely followed?
What is the Unite Union Book?
flashcards.back: A book published by the trade union 'Unite', based on BS 7671, containing a wealth of information for the practising electrician.

flashcards.front: What is the difference between a prohibition notice and an improvement notice?
flashcards.back: Prohibition: the activity or premises must not be used until rectified. Improvement: use can continue, but shortcomings must be rectified within a specified time period.

quiz.q: Which Regulations place duties on clients, designers and contractors throughout the life of a construction project?
quiz.why: The CDM Regulations place specific duties on clients, designers and contractors from inception to final demolition and removal.

quiz.q: Which Regulations cover chemicals, asbestos, cements, oils and sprays used in the workplace?
quiz.why: COSHH covers anything used in the workplace that could be considered hazardous to health, such as chemicals, asbestos, cements, oils and sprays.

quiz.q: Which Regulations cover the requirements for electricity supply in the United Kingdom?
quiz.why: The Electricity Safety, Quality and Continuity Regulations (ESQCR) cover the requirements for electricity supply in the UK.

quiz.q: Under the Personal Protective Equipment at Work Regulations, who is required to supply the PPE?
quiz.why: The employer supplies the PPE and the employee wears it.

quiz.q: Which Act replaced the Disability Discrimination Act (DDA) in most of the UK?
options: Health and Safety at Work etc. Act
Control of Noise at Work Act
quiz.why: The DDA has been repealed and replaced by the Equality Act 2010, except in Northern Ireland.

quiz.q: BS 7671 has closely followed which international standard?
quiz.why: The text states the regulations have closely followed the international standard IEC 60364.
BS 7671 is published by the IET.

quiz.q: Which IET Guidance Note covers Earthing and Bonding?
quiz.why: Guidance Note 8 is Earthing and Bonding, 3rd Edition.

quiz.q: Failure to comply with an Approved Code of Practice is:
options: not an offence in itself, but may contravene a statutory regulation
automatically a breach of BS 7671 only
quiz.why: Codes of practice do not normally have the force of law, but failure to comply may contravene a statutory regulation enforceable by law.

quiz.q: Which notice allows a work activity to continue but requires shortcomings to be rectified within a specified time?
quiz.why: An improvement notice lets the activity or premises continue to be used, but shortcomings must be rectified within a specified time period.

quiz.q: Which of these is a non-direct implication of breaking statutory Regulations?
quiz.why: Loss of reputation is a non-direct implication; fines, imprisonment and notices are direct.
